messages.content:
My first submission today failed. Kaggle showed only: “Notebook Threw Exception.” I had no clue what went wrong or how to fix it. I understand why Kaggle limits logs from private test data: detailed logs could reveal information about that data.

Could Kaggle first run each submission on a small sample of public data and show the full log? If a submission fails on private data, Kaggle could still show only a general error message. This would help me tell whether the problem is in my notebook or in Kaggle’s system, while keeping the private data safe.

My first submission today failed. Kaggle showed only:  **“Notebook Threw Exception.”** 
I had no clue what went wrong or how to fix it.
I understand why Kaggle limits logs from private test data: detailed logs could reveal information about that data. 

Could Kaggle first run each submission on **a small sample of public data and show the full log?**
If a submission fails on private data, Kaggle could still show only a general error message. This would help me tell whether the problem is in my notebook or in Kaggle’s system, while keeping the private data safe.

messages.content: Also it doesn't make sense to loose daily submission limit when the problem happens before the task actually started.
